scope: Finite registered zero-error capability ceilings for internal state, deterministic observation quotients, fixed-bit deterministic communication, fixed-architecture quantized threshold boundaries, finite deterministic update channels, exact linear protected-state subspaces, exhaustive planning horizons, unstructured verified search, verification false-adoption floors, active information acquisition, and social-observation identifiability. Every theorem applies only after all information, parameter, update, resource, and architecture channels named in its scope are frozen.
assumptions: capability claims are made against prospectively registered task, information, parameter and update interfaces
zero-error means every registered latent/task class must receive its required response, not merely high average accuracy
state-capacity claims exclude uncharged external memory or hidden side channels
observation-quotient claims use the complete information available before the registered decision; later probes/interventions must be incorporated before applying the quotient
communication claims use a noiseless deterministic fixed-bit one-way channel and no receiver side information correlated with the sender class
precision claims freeze architecture, decoder/codebook and every precision-bearing parameter slot; architecture growth or an uncharged high-precision side parameter changes the theorem
update-channel claims freeze the initial state and require every target-dependent persistent change to pass through the registered finite update alphabet
protected-rank claims are exact for linear protected-output maps, or local first-order statements after an explicit linearization; nonlinear/global invariance needs a separate theorem
planning claims meter exhaustive node inspections on a full finite b-ary tree with no pruning/oracle/merging
search claims are unstructured membership-query complexity with a perfect verifier and no candidate side information
verification claims use exchangeable defect locations for the hypergeometric floor and perfect distinct checks; adversarial zero-FA requires full coverage
information-acquisition claims count deterministic noiseless transcripts with bounded outcome alphabets and no free side information
social-observation claims apply the deterministic observation-quotient criterion to registered agent-model transcripts before held-out responses
evidence_class: P1 formal theorem family plus P2 exhaustive finite witnesses
strongest_parents: Blackwell comparison of experiments / deterministic sufficiency and garbling
finite hypothesis-class counting and quantized-network expressivity
finite-alphabet reachability / quantized control and information-constrained optimization
deterministic decision-tree/query complexity for unstructured search
acceptance sampling and the hypergeometric distribution
decision-tree / twenty-questions transcript counting and source coding
the already-registered deterministic observation-quotient ceiling plus statistical identifiability / inverse-planning theory-of-mind models
falsifier: A registered in-scope instance violates one of the stated ceilings while all theorem assumptions and all information/resource channels are checked exactly.

ceilings.quantity: K pairwise obligation-distinguishable history classes versus S available internal states.
ceilings.theorem: If K pairwise obligation-distinguishable histories must remain distinguishable after their common future observation interface and no other memory channel is available, zero-error success requires S >= K. Conversely, the finite delayed-label witness is realizable with S = K.
ceilings.bound: K <= S; equivalently the internal state identity carries at most log2(S) bits of distinction.
ceilings.strongest_parent: Myhill-Nerode theorem and distinguishing-set/state lower bounds.
assumptions: finite history quotient
no external memory or hidden side channel
future observations do not re-separate histories already merged by the controller
zero-error registered obligation
ceilings.negative_twin: K=3 delayed labels with S=2 states.
ceilings.falsifier: An exact in-scope controller with S<K states solves all K pairwise distinguishable obligations with zero error.

ceilings.quantity: Observation equivalence classes induced by the complete registered pre-decision observation map.
ceilings.theorem: For deterministic finite observation O:X->Z and required action g:X->A, with no later informative channel, a zero-error policy pi:Z->A exists iff g is constant on every fiber of O.
ceilings.bound: The required-action partition may not split an observation fiber; independently conditionable latent distinctions are bounded by the observation quotient.
ceilings.strongest_parent: Blackwell comparison/sufficiency; deterministic specialization of information garbling and data processing.
assumptions: finite deterministic observation map
complete pre-decision information channel is registered
no post-observation probe, intervention, memory, or side information refines the fiber
zero-error required action
ceilings.negative_twin: Two latent states share one observation but require different actions.
ceilings.falsifier: A policy using only the registered observation achieves zero error while assigning different required actions inside one observation fiber.

ceilings.quantity: K sender classes requiring distinct receiver actions versus a B-bit fixed-length one-way transcript.
ceilings.theorem: With no receiver side information correlated with the sender class, a deterministic zero-error protocol requires K <= 2^B. The bound is tight by injective coding whenever K <= 2^B.
ceilings.bound: B >= ceil(log2 K), or equivalently K <= 2^B distinct zero-error coordination classes.
ceilings.strongest_parent: Deterministic communication complexity; transcript/protocol-tree counting lower bound.
assumptions: finite sender coordination classes
noiseless deterministic fixed-length one-way communication
receiver has no correlated side information about sender class
distinct classes require distinct receiver actions
zero-error coordination
ceilings.negative_twin: K=5 coordination classes over B=2 bits.
ceilings.falsifier: An in-scope B-bit deterministic protocol coordinates K>2^B distinct required receiver actions with zero error.

ceilings.quantity: N ordered probe points, hence N+1 distinct one-threshold labelings, versus a frozen B-bit threshold code with at most 2^B decoded boundary placements.
ceilings.theorem: For a fixed one-dimensional threshold architecture whose only boundary-selecting degree of freedom is a frozen B-bit code, the represented threshold family contains at most min(2^B,N+1) distinct zero-error boundary placements on N ordered probe points. Covering all N+1 placements requires 2^B >= N+1, and this is tight.
ceilings.bound: Representable boundary placements <= min(2^B,N+1); complete threshold-family coverage requires B >= ceil(log2(N+1)).
ceilings.strongest_parent: Finite hypothesis-class/cardinality counting under parameter quantization; bounded specialization of quantized-network expressivity.
assumptions: one-dimensional one-threshold classifier family on a fixed finite ordered probe set
architecture and threshold decoder/codebook are frozen across the target family
all boundary-selecting precision-bearing parameters are included in the B-bit code
no architecture growth, additional high-precision parameter, or task-specific decoder rewrite
zero-error representation of the registered threshold labeling
ceilings.negative_twin: N=4 probe points expose five threshold placements but B=2 supplies at most four decoded placements.
ceilings.falsifier: A fixed in-scope B-bit threshold decoder realizes more than 2^B distinct boundary placements, or covers all N+1 placements when 2^B<N+1.

ceilings.quantity: K pairwise target-distinct successor states versus an A-symbol persistent update alphabet used for T update events.
ceilings.theorem: From a fixed initial persistent state, if every target-dependent persistent modification passes through a deterministic A-symbol update channel for at most T events and all other dynamics are target-independent, at most A^T target-distinct successor states can be selected. Guaranteeing K distinct targets requires K <= A^T; the bound is tight by injective transcript decoding.
ceilings.bound: K <= A^T; equivalently T >= ceil(log_A K) when A>1.
ceilings.strongest_parent: Finite-alphabet reachability/counting in quantized control and finite-rate information-constrained optimization.
assumptions: fixed initial persistent state
finite deterministic update alphabet of size A
at most T update events
all target-dependent persistent information enters only through the registered update symbols
no unmetered direct write, external memory mutation, target-correlated side channel, or architecture growth
zero-error target reachability
ceilings.negative_twin: A=2 update symbols for T=2 events expose four transcripts but K=5 distinct successor targets.
ceilings.falsifier: An in-scope deterministic A-symbol, T-event update channel selects K>A^T pairwise target-distinct persistent successor states from the same initial state.

ceilings.quantity: A D-dimensional mutable parameter vector and an exact linear protected-output map P of rank R.
ceilings.theorem: Exact zero-forgetting updates satisfy P*Delta=0 and therefore lie in ker(P), whose dimension is D-R by rank-nullity. Thus an S-dimensional family of independent linear plastic update directions can coexist with exact retention only if R+S <= D; this bound is tight.
ceilings.bound: plastic update dimension <= D-R, equivalently protected rank + independent plastic rank <= D.
ceilings.strongest_parent: Rank-nullity theorem; output-preserving/null-space projection methods in continual learning.
assumptions: fixed D-dimensional mutable vector space
protected old behavior is represented by an exact linear map P
retention requires P*Delta=0 exactly
plasticity is counted as the dimension of linearly independent admissible update directions
no architecture growth or auxiliary mutable state outside the registered D coordinates
ceilings.negative_twin: D=3 with rank(P)=2 leaves one protected null direction, so a two-dimensional independent plastic update family is impossible without changing protected outputs.
ceilings.falsifier: An exact in-scope protected map of rank R admits more than D-R linearly independent zero-forgetting update directions.

ceilings.quantity: Full b-ary planning tree, exhaustive node-inspection budget R, and guaranteed complete horizon h.
ceilings.theorem: In a full b-ary tree where any uninspected node through depth h may contain the only goal or obligation-changing event, a planner that guarantees complete zero-error coverage through depth h must inspect every node through that depth. The required node count is N(b,h)=h+1 for b=1 and (b^(h+1)-1)/(b-1) for b>1. The bound is tight by breadth-first exhaustive inspection.
ceilings.bound: N(b,h) <= R. For b>1, h <= floor(log_b(R(b-1)+1))-1; for b=1, h <= R-1.
ceilings.strongest_parent: Uninformed tree-search branching-factor complexity / exhaustive search.
assumptions: finite full b-ary tree and integer horizon h>=0
node inspection is the metered planning resource
any node through depth h may be adversarially decisive
no heuristic oracle, pruning certificate, state merging/transposition, or structural dominance rule
guarantee is complete worst-case coverage, not success on one lucky path
ceilings.negative_twin: A binary tree with R=14 cannot guarantee complete depth 3 because depth 3 contains 15 nodes including the root; R=15 is tight.
ceilings.falsifier: An in-scope planner guarantees complete depth h after inspecting fewer than N(b,h) nodes.

ceilings.quantity: N unstructured candidates, one hidden valid candidate, and Q deterministic membership-verifier queries.
ceilings.theorem: If exactly one of N candidates may be valid and validity of one candidate gives no information about any other, every deterministic algorithm that guarantees finding the valid candidate in the worst case requires Q>=N membership queries. With Q<N, an adversary places the unique valid candidate at an unqueried index. The bound is tight by querying all candidates.
ceilings.bound: Worst-case guaranteed verified-solution class size <= Q; complete guarantee over N candidates requires Q>=N.
ceilings.strongest_parent: Deterministic decision-tree/query complexity for unstructured search.
assumptions: finite candidate set with exactly one potentially valid location
validity membership oracle is exact
candidate identities are unstructured and checking one candidate gives no information about another
no generative shortcut, ordering promise, heuristic oracle, side information, or parallel unmetered verification
worst-case zero-error guarantee
ceilings.negative_twin: N=5 candidates with Q=4 queries; whichever four indices are checked, the fifth can be the unique valid candidate.
ceilings.falsifier: An in-scope deterministic search guarantees the unique valid candidate for all placements with Q<N queries.

ceilings.quantity: M obligation coordinates, exactly r defective coordinates chosen uniformly among all r-subsets, and q distinct perfect checks without replacement.
ceilings.theorem: Under exchangeable defect locations and no defect-location side information, any non-anticipating verifier that inspects q distinct coordinates and adopts iff all inspected coordinates pass misses every defect with probability C(M-q,r)/C(M,r), interpreted as zero when M-q<r. This is therefore the exact false-adoption probability for the registered model. In the distribution-free adversarial single-defect model, any q<M leaves an unchecked coordinate on which an invalid candidate can be placed, so zero worst-case false adoption requires q=M.
ceilings.bound: P_FA(q;M,r)=C(M-q,r)/C(M,r). For r=1, P_FA=(M-q)/M. Worst-case adversarial zero-FA requires q=M.
ceilings.strongest_parent: Acceptance sampling / hypergeometric sampling without replacement.
assumptions: finite M obligation coordinates and 1<=r<=M defects
the r-defect set is uniformly distributed over all r-subsets for the probabilistic bound
q distinct checks are chosen without defect-location side information
each checked defect is detected perfectly
candidate is adopted iff no checked coordinate fails
ceilings.negative_twin: M=10, r=1, q=8 has exact false-adoption probability 2/10; full q=10 verification has probability 0.
ceilings.falsifier: Under the registered exchangeable perfect-check model, measured exact enumeration disagrees with C(M-q,r)/C(M,r), or a q<M deterministic verifier guarantees zero false adoption against an adversarial single defect.

ceilings.quantity: K latent hypotheses, at most A outcomes per active query, at most q queries (or total budget B with uniform per-query cost c).
ceilings.theorem: Any deterministic adaptive q-query protocol with at most A outcomes per query has at most A^q complete transcripts, so zero-error identification of K latent hypotheses requires K <= A^q. Under uniform positive query cost c and total budget B, q <= floor(B/c), hence K <= A^floor(B/c). The count is tight when the registered query family can realize a separating A-ary code over the hypotheses.
ceilings.bound: K <= A^q; equivalently q >= ceil(log_A K) for A>1. With uniform cost: K <= A^floor(B/c).
ceilings.strongest_parent: Decision-tree leaf counting / twenty questions / finite source coding.
assumptions: finite K latent hypotheses
deterministic noiseless active queries with at most A outcomes each
at most q acquired answers, or uniform positive query cost c under total budget B
no free side information, passive observation or intervention outcome carrying additional target information
zero-error identification; tightness only when the query family can implement a separating code
ceilings.negative_twin: Five hypotheses with two binary queries expose at most four transcripts, so exact identification is impossible; three binary queries are sufficient in a rich separating-query family.
ceilings.falsifier: An in-scope deterministic q-query protocol identifies K>A^q hypotheses with zero error, or a B-budget protocol with uniform cost c identifies more than A^floor(B/c) hypotheses without another information channel.

ceilings.quantity: Finite hidden agent-model set Theta, registered social observation transcript tau(theta), and held-out required social response g(theta).
ceilings.theorem: Given only the registered deterministic transcript tau(theta), a zero-error social-response decoder exists iff g is constant on every transcript fiber tau^{-1}(t). Full hidden-model identification is possible iff tau is injective. Therefore two goal/belief models that are observationally equivalent under all registered social observations but require different held-out responses are not identifiable without an additional discriminating observation or assumption.
ceilings.bound: The held-out response partition cannot refine the transcript partition; full identifiable model classes <= number of distinct registered transcripts.
ceilings.strongest_parent: The F2 deterministic observation-quotient theorem (direct social-domain corollary), statistical identifiability, and inverse-planning/Bayesian theory-of-mind models that infer hidden goals/beliefs from observed actions.
assumptions: finite registered hidden agent-model set
complete deterministic social transcript available before the held-out response is frozen
no direct hidden-state label, private-state access or unregistered diagnostic interaction
required held-out social response g is fixed prospectively
zero-error deterministic theorem scope
ceilings.negative_twin: Two hidden models produce the same observed action in the base context but require different held-out predictions; no transcript-only decoder can answer both. A registered diagnostic probe that makes their transcripts differ restores identifiability.
ceilings.falsifier: A transcript-only decoder gives different correct responses to two models in the same transcript fiber, or fully identifies two hidden models with identical complete registered transcripts.
